notes.file_groups: 2007-2019 files are split by area and the area is only in the file name: Cabecera = municipal seats (urban), Resto = rural. Files not split are read as they are; 'Área' files duplicate Cabecera and are skipped.
notes.unify_columns: Some files spell the household ID differently (BOM, lowercase).
notes.factor: FEX_C18 (CNPV 2018 projection). In 2020 a separate projection file misses 8 new departments: FEX_C there.
notes.periods_per_year: Each monthly sample is expanded to the whole population.

notes.keep_rows: Only completed or partly completed interviews (RESULT 1-2), as INEI does: refusals, absences and empty dwellings have no data.
notes.keep_rows_any: Usual residents only, as INEI does: members not away 30+ days (P204 = 1, P205 = 2) and non-members present 30+ days (P204 = 2, P206 = 1). Every person module carries P204-P206.
notes.fill_missing: Literacy (P302) is only asked below completed primary: in the table that asks it, the people who were not asked and completed primary or more (P301A 4-11) take that level, which the value mapping counts as literate. Other blanks (e.g. 2020 phone interviews) stay Missing.

notes.parts: Households (dom) and persons (pes) are separate fixed-width files.

notes.derive_from_flags: Cooking fuel: S01016B ('most used') is only asked when 2+ fuels are used; otherwise the fuel is the only 'yes' among S01016A1-A5. S01016F holds it, and the mapping uses 'S01016B|S01016F'.

notes.row_ids_without_key: The 2006-2013 public files have no identifiers: rows get their own ID and persons are not linked to households.
notes.map_columns: ENHOGAR 2006 has provinces (ADMIN_DIVISION_2) but not regions.
notes.relative_weight_years: These years only have relative (normalized) weights, which average 1: shares are right but their sums are not population totals, so POPULATION / HOUSEHOLDS are left empty in the shares.
